thread:
incident-bot: PAGE: tenant=lumen dedicated-pool=eastus-2 severity=high — sudden p99 tail latency spike (tokens/sec high), paging oncall
jonah: acked, jumping in. seeing p50 ~45ms but p99 ~2.3s, error rate small but timeouts increasing :alarm_clock:
maria: i'm on metrics. requests are mostly short prompts (~8-40 tokens) at high qps. batch sizes reporting 1-3 tokens frequently. looks like scheduler not coalescing across connections.
prasanna: is this only lumen? any cross-tenant correlation?
jonah: isolating now — only tenant=lumen on that dedicated slice. no other tenants showing same pattern.
kevin: Lumen's SRE says they started a new marketing campaign ~30m ago, sudden spike in short queries. they're aware and throttling from their side as well.
maria: digging into scheduler knobs: max_batch_tokens for lumen is 512 (customized low). min_wait_ms is 2. current avg batch_tokens ~120 but because requests are short batch_count ~1-2 so overhead dominates.
jonah: hypothesis: low max_batch_tokens + aggressive per-tenant isolation -> tiny batches -> high per-request overhead. mitigation options: temporarily increase max_batch_tokens, increase min_wait_ms to allow more coalescing, enable aggressive_coalesce policy for this tenant, or route to backup model variant (smaller) until campaign cools.
prasanna: agree. prefer non-disruptive: raise max_batch_tokens and min_wait_ms, enable coalesce for 10% canary then 100% if metrics look good.
ops-bot: NOTE: runbook step 4 - "apply runtime knob" executed by oncall.
jonah: applying patch (canary 10%) now — command:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/tenants/lumen/overrides \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"overrides": {"inference.scheduler.max_batch_tokens": 2048, "inference.scheduler.min_wait_ms": 8, "inference.scheduler.coalesce_policy": "aggressive_coalesce"}, "canary_percent": 10}'
```
maria: metrics after 60s: canary hosts p99 down from 2.3s -> 420ms, p50 steady. overall cluster p99 drift 2.1s (because only 10%).
jonah: roll to 100% now if no regressions.
jonah: applying rollout 100%
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/tenants/lumen/overrides \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"overrides": {"inference.scheduler.max_batch_tokens": 2048, "inference.scheduler.min_wait_ms": 8, "inference.scheduler.coalesce_policy": "aggressive_coalesce"}, "canary_percent": 100}'
```
maria: cluster-wide p99 observed drop to ~380-450ms within 90s. error rate unchanged. CPU on slice up ~6% but still within limits. :white_check_mark:
kevin: Lumen SRE confirms client-side rate shaping paused campaign for ~15m, seeing improvements too. they appreciate the quick turn.
prasanna: set a temporary soft-shed on lumen queue for extreme bursts: add token_budget=20000 per-second to avoid queue meltdown if traffic spikes again. jonah — can you apply?
jonah: applying token_budget change now:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/tenants/lumen/overrides \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"overrides": {"inference.queue.token_budget_per_sec": 20000}}'
```
ops-bot: ALERT: token_budget override active for tenant=lumen by jonah.
maria: quick sanity: KV cache hit-rate unchanged (clients aren't using long-stream). batching efficiency improved: mean batch_count went from 1.6 -> 6.8.
jonah: leaving monitoring watch for 45m, will escalate to eng-runtime if p99 creeps back above 700ms.
prasanna: action items for postmortem: 1) review tenant-specific defaults (max_batch_tokens 512 was probably too small for bursty short prompts) 2) add auto-suggest to increase min_wait_ms when batch_count is low 3) consider adaptive per-tenant coalescing based on prompt length distribution 4) document procedure for token_budget soft-shed.
kevin: i'll open a support ticket for Lumen and schedule a joint post-incident call. will include timeline and applied knobs.
jonah: paging handoff in 30m to night SRE — i'll summarize: applied max_batch_tokens=2048, min_wait_ms=8, coalesce policy aggressive, token_budget=20000, canary->100% rolled, p99 improved ~5x. leaving monitoring.
maria: saving metrics snapshot and logs: attached to incident ticket (link https://tickets.redwood/internal/INC-76432). snippet: 
```
before: p99=2300ms, batch_count=1.6, avg_tokens=16
after:  p99=420ms,  batch_count=6.8, avg_tokens=18
```
jonah: note for oncall: if p99 rises again, temp rollback option is to set coalesce_policy back to "conservative" and enable route-fallback to smaller model (gpt-small-2024) for 20% of traffic. both are quick toggles.
prasanna: will we add a policy to auto-increase max_batch_tokens when median prompt token < 64 and batch_count < 3 for >30s? seems useful.
maria: filed RFC draft in eng-runtime board, will PR a simple heuristic.
kevin: Lumen requests a short write-up for SLG — i'll draft and loop in maria for the metrics.
jonah: handing off to night team: @oncall-night please monitor p99 and token_budget consumption. escalate to eng-runtime if CPU > 80% on dedicated slice.
ops-bot: Handoff reminder: create incident summary, assign to eng-runtime and customer-success.
jonah: thanks everyone. standby for any regressions. :coffee:
